finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the POST 'feed' parameter is passed unvalidated to file_get_contents, which fetches arbitrary URLs and wrapper schemes (http, https, ftp, file, php). The response length is echoed back, giving an oracle for internal hosts and ports.
finding.source: $_POST['feed'] (import.php:11), reachable by any POST containing 'feed' with no authentication.

trace.note: session_start(); no authentication check on this path
Branch taken on any POST where isset($_POST['feed'])
Raw attacker value passed to file_get_contents as the URL
strlen($xml) echoed to the client, giving a response-size oracle

finding.guards_checked: None on this path: no authentication, no scheme allowlist, no host or IP allowlist (no private, loopback, or metadata-address blocking), no port restriction, no redirect control, no timeout or size limit. The value is used as-is.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check on the feed path is the `REQUEST_METHOD === 'POST' && isset($_POST['feed'])` branch condition (import.php:11), which is not validation. require_admin() (import.php:4-9) is only called on the set_webhook branch (line 18), not the feed branch. No scheme, host, IP, port, or size check exists between line 11 and the sink at line 12.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled $_POST['feed'] at import.php:11 reaches file_get_contents() unvalidated at import.php:12 with no authentication (require_admin is not called on this path), and strlen($xml) is echoed at import.php:13, so the candidate's trace is accurate and the SSRF is unguarded. One caveat outside the code: the impact of non-HTTP wrappers depends on the PHP config (allow_url_fopen, allow_url_include), which I could not check from the directory.

finding.claim: Admin-gated blind SSRF: the POST 'set_webhook' parameter is passed unvalidated to curl_init and curl_exec, so an admin session can make the server issue requests to arbitrary internal or external targets. The response body is discarded.

trace.note: Branch taken on any POST where isset($_POST['set_webhook'])
Raw attacker value copied into $hook without validation
curl_init($hook) creates the handle with the unvalidated URL
curl_exec performs the request; the result is not echoed, so the SSRF is blind (only 'ok' is returned at line 23)

finding.guards_checked: require_admin() session check only (import.php:4-9, 18). No URL scheme, host, or IP validation and no CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS restriction. CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION is not set, so redirects are not followed by default. Severity is lower because exploitation requires an admin session.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() session check at import.php:4-9, invoked at import.php:18 (exits 403 unless $_SESSION['is_admin'] is non-empty). No URL scheme, host, or IP validation and no CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS restriction on the path to curl_init at import.php:20.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code (import.php:17-22), but the value at import.php:19 is only reachable after the admin-session gate at import.php:18, so the source is not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker, which the verification rubric requires for a CONFIRMED finding. Separately, the unauthenticated branch at import.php:11-12 (file_get_contents($_POST['feed'])) is outside this candidate and should be checked as its own finding.
